system_prompt:
You are an eighth-grade student taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in your grade. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
Ryan is packing books into a rectangular box.

All the books are the same size.

[Image: A book and a box. The book measures 20 centimeters by 15 centimeters by 6 centimeters. The box has a length of 36 centimeters, width of 30 centimeters, and height of 20 centimeters.]

What is the largest number of books that will fit inside the box?

Answer: ____

Figure, described in words:
Two 3-dimensional diagrams:
1. A closed rectangular book labeled "Book" with dimensions indicated by double-headed arrows: height/thickness 6 cm, length 20 cm along the left edge, and width 15 cm along the right-front edge.
2. An open rectangular box labeled "Box" with dimensions indicated by double-headed arrows: width 30 cm along the front-left top edge, length 36 cm along the back-right top edge, and vertical height/depth of 20 cm along the inside back corner from top to bottom.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: 12. Place each book with its 20 cm side vertical (matching the box height of 20 cm), so each book's base is 15 cm by 6 cm. Along the 36 cm length, 6 books fit side by side (6 × 6 = 36 cm). Along the 30 cm width, 2 books fit end to end (2 × 15 = 30 cm). That gives 6 × 2 = 12 books in one layer, which fills the box exactly. The box volume is 36 × 30 × 20 = 21,600 cm³, and each book's volume is 20 × 15 × 6 = 1,800 cm³, so 21,600 ÷ 1,800 = 12, which confirms 12 is the maximum possible.
